doc.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: Thirds in the bass and guitar-based writing today
summary: Conniff says many young writers write from guitar and miss the beauty of the third in the bass he learned from Tchaikovsky; Rowe cites Bernstein.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: No, no, no, no. Larry King. He had Eric Clapton on. And he was playing guitar, and I think except the way I heard him and his writings with the guitar, mainly today, well a point I want to make is a lot of today’s music is being written by guitar players. You can’t — with the guitar you miss the beauty of a Tchaikovsky, like [scats], you know the third in the bass. The seventh and the bass. With a guitar you always have the tonic in the bass. And I think that’s missing a little bit in the younger writers today. They write with the guitar. They need to study those classics and see the beauty, the great sound of a third in the bass and not doubled in the harmony. You know, leave the third out in the harmony. It’s only down there. There’s something about that, it just moves me, I don’t know.

It’s interesting you mention that, because if you look at — recently I was looking at some of the music from “West Side Story,” and “One Hand One Heart.” And that’s what Bernstein did. He had very simple chords, but he would put the third in the bass, and it changed the whole thing, it gave it a real beautiful effect.

Well if you took Tchaikovsky and put the melody in the bass line, you’ve practically got a composition and a score like this you know. But with today’s writers, everything’s going like this. But there’s something about that contrary motion and the movement of the bass, it’s great. But I learned that from breaking those scores down, you know, and I thought wow, what a sound, that’s great, that’s how they do that, huh? And I’d hunt, and wait a minute now, have an F chord and there would be an A in the bass, and I’d be looking, it must be, he’s got guys way up in there, he must have an A somewhere there. And I’d look at it — no A. No A. It’s only down in the bass.
